SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality franchise with strong brand, extensive store network (~4,900+ locations), and leading North American coatings market position. However, the near-term picture is mixed. Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth (revenue +6.8%, EPS +7.5%) but significant QoQ declines (revenue -10.9%, EPS -35.8%) reflecting normal seasonality in a Q1-heavy business. Operating cash flow was weak at $139M vs $1.3B in Q3 2025, though this is partly seasonal. The balance sheet carries meaningful leverage (debt/equity ~2.1x, total debt $9.3B vs equity $4.4B). Valuation at P/E ~29.6x is near the low end of its 12-month range (28.0-37.1), suggesting the stock has de-rated somewhat from peak multiples. P/B at 17.4x is also at the lower end of its range (16.4-21.4). The Q2 earnings report expected July 28 is a near-term catalyst — consensus expects $3.56 EPS (+5.3% YoY) and $6.62B revenue, with Zacks Earnings ESP of +0.94% suggesting a likely beat. Management raised FY2026 guidance to $11.50-$11.90 EPS. However, rising interest rates (10Y at 4.71%, up from 4.35 in late April) and elevated oil prices ($93/bbl) create headwinds for the housing/renovation cycle that drives demand. The lead paint litigation risk, while largely historical, remains a disclosed contingent liability. Overall, a solid but not exceptional setup — good franchise at a fair-to-slightly-cheap valuation with a modest near-term catalyst.
